### Latest AKR papercuts separate into verified fixes and four live clusters

`verified` · `@akr.assessment.papercut-reconciliation-2026-08-11/2` · scope `path "crates/akr-cli/**"`, `path "crates/akr-core/**"`, `path "crates/akr-mcp/**"`, `path "docs/**"`, `path "spec/**"`

Reconciliation of @akr.papercut.collated-18-papercuts-from-evidence-intake/1 at
ff0170d6ffe2f5b1d55eb63f6c8ae469bd36cff6 produced these dispositions.

RESOLVED AND EVIDENCED: the knowledge.explain crash is covered by CLI/MCP differential
tests; subject-scoped papercut collation, MCP budget handling and validation paging,
stale search-cache refresh, all generated view renderers, Git history batching, strict
AKR-G004 handling, and co-committed evidence/post-commit view convergence are covered by
their existing decisions and passing evidence. The decisions
@akr.decision.papercut-subject-and-collation/2 and
@akr.decision.mcp-budgeted-and-instrumented/2 were implemented but accidentally left
proposed and should be active. The two local post-commit papercuts are resolved by
ff0170d6.

PARTIALLY RESOLVED, RETAINED IN AUTHORING CONTRACTS: papercut namespace requirements
are now in CLI help and the MCP schema; CLI writes now name `akr build` when the lock
becomes stale; required slots are present in the kind schema. The remaining reports
are still valid because optional slot types, per-kind relations, AKR-T002 suggestions,
observation provenance, malformed/zero-match scope globs, MCP lock-remedy output,
`--from` shape, and CLI/MCP naming are not yet consistently discoverable.

LIVE CORRECTNESS/RELIABILITY: recurrent connector-level Transport closed reports are
not disproved by the in-memory thousand-frame protocol test; they require installed
subprocess stress. MCP revise currently constructs a replacement state but the core
sealed-revision path resets the new head to the class initial state unless Edits.state
is separately set, matching the ready-to-active and active-decision reports. Context
still rejects pinned goals while get accepts them, and different-key supersession is
still advertised by the MCP schema but rejected by the implementation.

TRACKED: the surviving work is now represented by
@akr.work.mcp-transport-reliability,
@akr.work.authoring-contracts,
@akr.work.revise-lifecycle-semantics, and
@akr.work.reference-supersession-consistency.

## Evidence

### Three rmcp major versions (1.8.0, 2.2.0, 3.1.4) drive akr-mcp from outside the workspace and all accept every response: protocol negotiation echoes each requested version, server/discover offers all five published versions on 3.x, 23 tools list, and all 24 tool calls deserialise. Reintroducing each historical defect fails it on exactly the generation that rejected it in the field -- resultType 'tool' fails 3.x with 'Unexpected response type' while 1.x and 2.x pass, reproducing Codex 0.147 on 13 August versus 0.149 on the 21st. Reported alongside: 23 of 23 declared outputSchemas constrain nothing, so validating payloads against them cannot currently fail.

### A real rmcp 3.1.2 client now connects to akr-mcp on both lifecycles. Before: the Auto (pre-initialize server/discover) path failed 'expect initialized result' because the discovery response was an initialize result under a discovery method name, and the post-initialize peer.discover() path failed 'Unexpected response type' - the error Codex 0.149 reported. After: Auto connects at 2026-07-28 and legacy+discover() connects at 2025-11-25, both listing 23 tools, with supportedVersions ['2026-07-28','2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26','2024-11-05']. Adding 2025-11-25 also stops every rmcp 3.x host being silently answered 2024-11-05.

### a_current_index_search_does_not_invoke_git passed in a 10-test run of the akr-cli search suite. It builds the index, then runs akr search with PATH pointed at an empty directory, so a git subprocess could not be found if one were attempted; the command exits 0 and returns results. The fast path is structurally git-free rather than merely quick, and this pass's akr-cli and akr-mcp changes did not disturb it.
